My tough little vinnirex can't keep this up any longer, the khanith are getting bolder each night and I don't know if my bloomux 
herd will make it to the season's harvest. Looking for a Traveler to come help keep my herd safe. 
Job: Defend a bloomux herd from an incoming khanith attack for a full night. Success: At least 1 bloomux survives.
Scenario: Five bloomux rest on a fi eld of flowers for a full night. Two Tamed vinnirex accompany the Traveler, 
both the vinnirex and bloomux treat them as an ally. Four separate waves of 1d6+3 khanith attack throughout 
the length of the night.
A sickening crimson taint has infected our grove, the trees bleed. All the animals, even our own pack beasts, have become 
wildly violent the moment they step into that bloody forest. Someone has to root out this disease before the whole of the 
Wealdwoods goes mad.
Job: A grove of trees has turned crimson and is weeping a blood colored sap. Creatures in the area are growing 
aggressive and will attack others on sight. Success: Investigate and remove what has caused this infection. 
Scenario: When entering the crimson grove, and every hour spent in the grove, roll on the Wealdwoods 
Scavengers Table and fi ght any potential encounters. To discover what has caused the infection, roll a DC 16 
Intelligence (Nature) check. Success: Th e Traveler discovers that a unique mushroom has infected one tree and 
once pulled from the trunk, the Wealdwoods will heal within a 1d4 days. Failure: Th e infection goes unchecked 
and all people leave the vicinity as the violent creatures are too lethal.
Crimson Fungus Infected Beasts • Variant Additions: Any Beasts within 100 ft. of the infected tree will 
aggressively attack any species that is not their own.
Unreasoning Madness Advantage on Wisdom Saving Th rows.
Manic Rage Add their Profi ciency Bonus to any Damage on melee attack rolls.
Senseless Anger Th ey gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Our little village only survives because of our lexati. Something or someone has been taking them from their perches at night, 
please fi nd them, I fear the worst!
Job: Search the whereabouts of the lost lexati within the Wealdwoods. Success: Free them before they are slain.
Scenario: Follow the signs of struggle and listen for the cries of the distraught creatures, DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) 
check. Th e Tracking roll can be attempted a total of three times. Success: Th e Traveler fi nds the lexati. Failure:
Th e Traveler loses an hour of tracking and rolls on the Wealdwoods Scavengers Table and fi ghts any potential 
encounters. Th e lexati are found to be at the top of a massive tree deep in the Wealdwoods, 4d4 basilospri guard 
the lexati to feed to their young. Lexati will treat the Traveler as an ally and the basilospri will randomly attack 
either the Travelers or their captive lexati, when all basilospri are slain, the lexati will glide away back to the 
village.

No merchant caravans have visited our small isolated village in many moons. Worried, we traveled out along the trade roads 
and found a caravan waylaid and slaughtered. Long claw marks and dried blood are all the remained of the supplies.
Job:  An especially aggressive grahknash is waylaying caravans with impunity. Success: Venture out and hunt 
down the beast before it strikes fi rst. 
Marauding Grahknash • Variant Additions: + 2 STR, +2 CON, +24 HP, +10 Movement Speed
BONUS ACTION - Voracious Th e marauding grahknash can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that 
it can see.
Our waters have gone afoul, our fi shermen bring home only rotten and decaying fi sh, and a rank smell has sickened our folk. 
We need a Traveler to root out the source of this malady that is tainting our home. 
Job:  A strain of diseased ruske are poisoning the water. Success: Slay all 4d6 Pestilent Ruske.
Pestilent Ruske • Variant Additions: + 4 CON, +12 HP, Resistance: Poison
Infected Lance (replaces Chitin Lance) Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d6 + 1) Poison 
damage. If the ruske moved at least 10 ft. toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 
7 (2d6) Piercing damage.
Never seen anything like it, ripped right through a family of aphistus before they could even squawk out a warning. I think 
it was a sacrissian from the look of those horns, but I've never seen one this deep in the Wealdwoods. 
Job:  An especially fi erce sacrissian is upending the balance between predator and prey, either force it out from 
the Wealdwoods or slay it. Success: Slay or incapacitate the Savage Sacrissian.
Savage Sacrissian • Variant Additions: +2 AC, +3 WIS, +10 Movement Speed
Multiattack Th e sacrissian makes four attacks, it can use its Toothed Beak, Foreclaws or Crown of Horns in 
any combination.

Traveler needed. Every time we set sail those thrice-cursed crustaceans rip through our board and sail with their damnable 
stones. We can hardly feed our own if we cannot fi sh beyond the surf.
Job: Defend a fi shing vessel for a full hour on the open seas as they attempt to fi sh. Success: At least 1 Fisherman 
survives the full hour. 
Scenario: Every 10 minutes roll a 1d4, on a 1 an arkiopti appears to attack the fi shing vessel. Six Fishermen 
are focused on casting their lines and nets. Arkiopti randomly attack Travelers and Fisherman on each turn 
of combat. 
Fishermen: Medium Humanoid, AC 10, Hp 4 (1d8), STR 10, DEX 10, CON 10, INT 10, WIS 10, CHA 10.

Bastion

We found a half starved and full mad sailor washed up ashore ranting about her priceless sextant, she was unsure of where her 
vessel crashed among the rocks and coral out at Windward. If a Traveler is looking to help, please bring back her precious tool. 
Job: Search for a wrecked scouting vessel. Success: Escape with the lost sextant. 
Scenario: Search for the vessel out on the multitude of islands and coral outcroppings, DC 16 Wisdom (Survival) 
check.Th e Tracking roll can be attempted a total of three times. Success: Th e Traveler fi nds the stranded scouting 
vessel. Failure: Th e Traveler loses an hour of tracking and rolls on the Strands Scavengers Table and fi ghts any 
potential encounters. Upon discovery, the sextant can be found near the prow, but 1d3 nicalliath infest the 
vessel and will attack the Traveler on sight.
Strands
Windward
Diffi culty: Hard
Someone has to fi nd my daughter Daedriss! It has been three days since she wandered off from our village, she was last seen 
going west to the caverns at dawn and our best trackers have found nothing. Please we need someone before its too late.
Job: Track down and bring home the child. Success: Daedriss survives the encounter and is brought back home 
to her village.
Scenario: Search the Umbrawells caves for signs of the missing child, DC 14 Wisdom (Survival) check. Th e 
Tracking roll can be attempted a total of three times. Success: Th e Traveler fi nds the girl within a cavern. Failure:
Th e Traveler loses an hour of tracking and rolls on the Umbrawells Scavengers Table and fi ghts any potential 
encounters. Upon discovery, the girl has been taken in by a family of 3d3 gorr, who are beset by an aggressive 
pack of 1d6+3 mollucite encroaching within their cave. Th e gorr and Daedriss will treat the Traveler as an ally 
if the Traveler combats the group of mollucite.
A Traveler came through our town, speaking of a peaceful meadow with a mirror-like pond not far beyond our borders, a true 
safe haven from the dangerous wilds that surround us. We're requesting the help of another Traveler to journey out and create 
a map of this so called meadow. 
Job: Travel through the ceaseless swamps to fi nd the meadow. Success: Marking a map along the way to help the 
villagers know of its location.
Scenario: Search for the meadow among the marshes, DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check. Th e Tracking roll can be 
attempted a total of three times. Success: Th e Traveler fi nds the peaceful meadow. Failure: Th e Traveler loses an 
hour of tracking and is beset upon by 1d3 solmundis and fi ghts these encounters. Upon discovery, the Traveler 
is overcome with a sense of serenity and peace as they step into a quiet clearing with a small group of gurubara 
basking in the water. Th e meadow's peace is soon shattered by an invading herd of 3d3 fennfi stle. If the Traveler 
chooses to engage and combat the fennfi stle, the gurubara will treat the Traveler as an ally in the encounter.

Th e ground has been rumbling something fi erce this last fortnight and we loggers fear the worse. We need a Traveler to 
investigate what is happening within our glades.
Job: Barricade an opening in the earth with fallen logs. Success: Place eight logs over the hole to deter the 
invading tormull.
Scenario: Th e ground has been rumbling within a clearing in the woods. Eventually the ground gives way and 
tormull charge out of a 10 x 10 ft. round hole. Initially 1d4+1 tormull appear and roll a 1d4 every subsequent 
6 minutes for more to escape the cave opening. Block the cave opening by placing 10 ft. long logs that lay 
in stacks around the clearing. DC 10 Strength test to pick up a log, while holding a log a Travelers speed is 
reduced to 5 ft. and they cannot use their arms while holding onto one. 
Time and time again our caravans have been waylaid by a pack of voracious draffers. We need a strong arm and fi erce guard 
to make our next trip.
Job: Stand atop a closed caravan and defend it from predatory draffers. Success: At least one pack beast must 
survive a full hour of travel.
Scenario: A pack beast drawn caravan is crossing the open plains of the Tundrus at 60 ft. per minute. Either 
use rutort or equivalent Beasts of Burden (horse, ox, etc.). When traveling begins, 1d6+2 draffers appear at the 
outskirts and run in to attack. Success: At least 1 Beast of Burden survives the full hour.

I keep hearing the most mournful of cries coming from that cursed dark chasm, I can't imagine what could be making such a 
pitiful call for help. If there are any Travelers with a caring spirit to help those in pain, something out there needs you. 
Job: Track down and defend a wounded omaterssum against attacking skith. Success: Th e omaterssum survives 
the encounter.
Scenario: Track a wounded omaterssum into the caves, DC 15 Wisdom (Survival) check. Th e Tracking roll can 
be attempted a total of three times before the wounded omaterssum is slain. Success: Th e Traveler fi nds the 
wounded omaterssum being attacked by 1d6+1 skith. Failure: Th e Traveler loses an hour of tracking and rolls on 
the Umbrawells Scavengers Table and fi ghts any potential encounters.
Wounded Omaterssum: 30/75 HP remaining, will treat the Traveler as an ally if they attack the skith.
